question: Why did revolutionary France keep the metre but give up the ten-hour day?
answer: Because the metre solved a problem and decimal time created one. Towns across France had their own pounds and grain measures, so trade gained from one standard; a ten-hour day solved nothing and needed new clocks. Compulsory from September 1794, it was suspended in April 1795 by the law that named the metre and gram.
move: A reform survives when it removes a cost people already feel.
source: Alder, The Measure of All Things, 2002
reference: Alder, The Measure of All Things: The Seven-Year Odyssey and Hidden Error That Transformed the World, Free Press, 2002
